docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to LabPress are documented in this file.

The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project follows Semantic Versioning. Versions are ordered from newest to oldest.

LabPress 1.1.1 is a maintenance and integration release. It does not add a new database schema or a new top-level module; instead, it tightens the boundary between the core and plugins, makes the admin language setting genuinely independent from the frontend, and completes the public navigation with an account entry.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Cleaner i18n boundary. Core language packs now contain only framework-owned strings. Plugin language files are loaded only through an explicit plugin:{slug} module, so a plugin can no longer overwrite a core label by accident.
  • Independent admin language. The admin panel can use its own locale, persisted in ml_admin_locale, without changing the visitor-facing lang cookie. The switch is available on the login page and in the admin topbar.
  • Correct first-request locale resolution. loadPlugins() now runs before the early getLocale() call. A ?lang=zh_CN request therefore reaches the plugin's admin_locale filter instead of caching the site default for the whole request.
  • Public account entry. The front-end navigation now shows a Sign in button for guests and the signed-in username for administrators. The username links to the dashboard and exposes a hover menu of permitted admin pages.
  • Front-end-safe login redirect. A login started from the public homepage can return to the homepage after success instead of always landing in /admin/index.php.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Added the admin_locale filter in getLocale(). Signature: applyFilters('admin_locale', $defaultLocale, $availableLocales). The filter must return a locale directory name; invalid or non-string values fall back to the site default.
  • Added the admin_topbar_actions action in the admin topbar. Plugins can render compact controls without replacing the whole topbar template.
  • Added Dynamic Multi-Language 2.0.2 with backend language selection on admin/login.php and in the admin topbar.
  • Added the ml_admin_locale session and cookie preference. Resolution order is request lang, session value, cookie value, then the core site default.
  • Added the public navigation account entry in includes/header.php:
  • guests see a Sign in button linking to admin/login.php?redirect=home;
  • authenticated users see $_SESSION['user'];
  • the username links directly to admin/index.php;
  • hovering or keyboard-focusing the username opens a menu with dashboard, publications, projects, tools, and research-news shortcuts;
  • entries that require a permission the current user does not have are not rendered.
  • Added redirect=home handling in admin/login.php, including a hidden form field and the existing login_redirect_url filter. Only the literal value home is treated as a homepage redirect, so the parameter cannot be used as an open redirect.
  • Added the front-end language keys nav_login, nav_admin, nav_admin_dashboard, nav_admin_publications, nav_admin_projects, nav_admin_tools, and nav_admin_news in both zh_CN and en_US.
  • Added regression notes for the locale-order fix in docs/i18n/core-lang.md and docs/changelog.md.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Core __() no longer scans and merges every active plugin's language file. It loads:
  • languages/{locale}/{module}.php for core modules; or
  • plugins/{slug}/languages/{locale}.php when the caller explicitly uses plugin:{slug}.
  • Plugin language keys are no longer part of the global core namespace. A plugin must call __('key', 'plugin:plugin-slug') for its own strings, and should still use a unique prefix such as ml_, fi_, or acme_.
  • Dynamic Multi-Language registers its admin menu title with __('ml_plugin_name', 'plugin:dynamic-multilang') instead of relying on an implicit merge.
  • Admin JavaScript for project management, news management, plugin market, and plugin installation now reads language objects injected by PHP rather than embedding Chinese labels in JS source.
  • The admin language policy is now explicitly plugin-owned. The core supplies only the admin_locale filter and a safe fallback; without the plugin, the admin panel follows the site default language.
  • The front-end header is now the single source of truth for the account entry. Because it is shared by all public pages, the entry is not limited to index.php.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Fixed the admin language switch being ignored on the first request. getLocale() previously ran before loadPlugins(), so the admin_locale filter did not exist and the site default locale was cached in the static $locale variable. Locale resolution now runs after plugin loading.
  • Fixed the Dynamic Multi-Language admin page reading a non-existent original_content key; it now uses ml_original_content.
  • Fixed missing ml_no_translations_yet interface text in the plugin language packs.
  • Fixed hard-coded 个 and 无 strings in the tool-version admin view; the page now uses the count_unit and none core keys.
  • Fixed the account dropdown inheriting the main navigation's flex layout; the nested list is explicitly rendered as a vertical block.
  • Fixed the public login link losing its return target after form submission; the hidden redirect field preserves home.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Reworked the v1.1.1 changelog into a release note with upgrade and verification steps.
  • Documented the core/plugin language boundary, the admin_locale contract, the login-page and topbar switchers, and the locale-order regression.
  • Added Mermaid diagrams for the request lifecycle, locale resolution, plugin lifecycle, translation flow, and content-management workflows.
  • Corrected stale navigation paths and installation section numbering.

docs.title: Upgrade Notes
docs.text:
1. Back up first. Export the MySQL database and archive includes/config.php. The file is intentionally untracked or skip-worktree in many deployments and must not be overwritten by a pull.
  2. Update the working tree. On the server, run git pull from the project root. If the server has local edits that are known to be disposable, stash them first; do not run git reset --hard on a tree that contains a protected includes/config.php.
  3. Confirm the plugin version. Open Plugins → Installed Plugins and verify that Dynamic Multi-Language reports 2.0.2. If the plugin is active but its files are older, replace the plugin directory from the release package and reactivate it.
  4. Clear opcache if applicable. If PHP OPcache is enabled, reload PHP-FPM or restart the pool so the new includes/functions.php is compiled. A stale opcode cache can make the language fix appear not to work.
  5. Do not copy old plugin language files into languages/. Plugin strings must stay inside the plugin. Moving them into the core pack reintroduces key collisions.
  6. Re-login once. The account entry reads $_SESSION['user']; after deployment, sign out and sign in again so the public header can render the username.

No database migration is required for 1.1.1. Existing ml_translations, plugins, and content tables remain compatible.

docs.title: Verification Checklist
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Deploy 1.1.1] --> B[Open /admin/login.php?lang=zh_CN]
    B --> C{HTML lang is zh-CN?}
    C -- No --> D[Check loadPlugins order and OPcache]
    C -- Yes --> E[Switch to English and back]
    E --> F[Open frontend in another tab]
    F --> G[Frontend language must remain independent]
    G --> H[Sign in from homepage]
    H --> I{Returned to homepage?}
    I -- No --> J[Check hidden redirect field]
    I -- Yes --> K[Username appears in nav bar]
    K --> L[Hover username: admin links open]
    L --> M{Only permitted links visible?}
    M -- No --> N[Check permissions array in session]
    M -- Yes --> O[Release verified]
  • curl -s 'https://your-site/admin/login.php?lang=zh_CN' | grep '<html' should show lang="zh-CN" (or the locale attribute used by the current template).
  • The language switch must survive a reload and must not change the public site's language.
  • The public Sign in button must appear only when no user session exists.
  • After login from the homepage, the browser must return to /index.php, not to /admin/index.php.
  • The username menu must show Dashboard for every authenticated user and hide publication/project/tool/news entries that the account cannot access.
  • The plugin can be deactivated without breaking the admin panel; the backend then falls back to the site default language.

The login-page switcher added by Dynamic Multi-Language 2.0.2. The URL carries ?lang=zh_CN; the interface and <html lang> must both be Chinese, not only the address bar.

docs.title: Compatibility and Boundaries
docs.text: Item 1.1.1 status PHP 7.4 or newer; PHP 8.x supported by the code path used in this release MySQL / MariaDB MySQL 5.7+ / MariaDB 10.3+ Database migration None Plugin API admin_locale filter and admin_topbar_actions action are additive Language packs Core packs own framework strings; plugin packs must use plugin:{slug} Front-end account menu Requires a valid $_SESSION['user'] and the hasPermission() helper Screenshots v1.1.1 admin dashboard and login captures are refreshed; older module captures remain in place until the host is reachable again

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Translation function __() now supports explicit plugin language loading with the plugin: prefix. Plugin authors can call __('key', 'plugin:plugin-slug') to load translations from a specific plugin without merging them into the core namespace.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Plugin language files are loaded only when explicitly requested or during the legacy scan of active plugins. The scan sanitizes plugin slugs before constructing file paths.
  • Dynamic Multi-Language language keys use the ml_ prefix to avoid collisions with core keys.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Fixed an issue where Dynamic Multi-Language keys such as plugin_name, about_us, and research_title overwrote core language keys and produced incorrect admin labels.
  • Fixed the plugin language file path when using the explicit plugin: module prefix.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • Documented the explicit plugin: syntax and the recommended key-prefix convention.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Initial stable release of LabPress, an open-source academic CMS for research laboratories.
  • Dynamic content management for About Us, research directions, statistics, and navigation menus.
  • Built-in academic modules for publications, projects, research news, tools, and tool versions.
  • Hook-driven plugin system with WordPress-style actions and filters.
  • Two-layer internationalization: static language packs plus the Dynamic Multi-Language plugin for database content.
  • Markdown editing with EasyMDE and live preview.
  • Pure PHP + MySQL runtime with no framework, Composer, or build step.
  • Plugin installation, activation, update, and uninstallation from the admin panel.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
• Clone or download the repository.
  • Copy includes/config-sample.php to includes/config.php and set the database credentials.
  • Import labpressexample.sql into MySQL.
  • Grant write permissions to uploads/ and plugins/.
  • Open / for the frontend and /admin for the panel.

docs.title: Important
docs.text:
• Change the default root / lab123456 credentials immediately after the first login.
  • LabPress is distributed under GPL-3.0.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to contribute to the LabPress project. It covers reporting issues, proposing changes, setting up a development environment, following code conventions, and submitting pull requests.

The goal is to make the contribution process clear and predictable while maintaining the quality and consistency of the project.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
LabPress is an open-source project released under the GNU General Public License v3.0. Contributions are welcome from anyone, including bug reports, feature suggestions, documentation improvements, and code changes.

The project is hosted on GitHub:

https://github.com/GuiHui-huimy/LabPress

All contributions should be submitted through GitHub Issues and Pull Requests.

flowchart TD
    A[Fork or branch] --> B[Focused change]
    B --> C[php -l]
    C --> D[Manual test]
    D --> E[Update docs]
    E --> F[Pull request]
    F --> G[Review]
    G -->|Changes requested| B
    G -->|Approved| H[Merge]

docs.title: 2. Code of Conduct
docs.text:
All contributors are expected to follow the project’s Code of Conduct. The full text is available in the CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md file in the repository root.

The Code of Conduct establishes basic expectations for respectful communication and professional behavior. Please read it before participating in discussions or submitting contributions.

docs.title: 3. Reporting Issues
docs.text: Issues are used to report bugs, request features, or suggest improvements.

docs.title: 3.1 Bug Reports
docs.text:
When reporting a bug, include as much relevant information as possible:

  • LabPress version or commit hash.
  • PHP version and MySQL version.
  • Web server and hosting environment, if relevant.
  • Steps to reproduce the problem.
  • Expected behavior and actual behavior.
  • Any relevant error messages or screenshots.

A clear bug report helps maintainers understand and fix the problem faster.

docs.title: 3.2 Feature Requests
docs.text:
Feature requests should describe the problem that the feature would solve rather than only the desired solution. Include:

  • The use case or scenario.
  • Why the current behavior is insufficient.
  • How the proposed change would improve the system.
  • Any relevant examples or references.

docs.title: 3.3 Security Issues
docs.text: Do not report security vulnerabilities through public issues. Instead, follow the process described in SECURITY.md. Security reports are handled privately until a fix is ready.

docs.title: 4. Development Setup
docs.text: Contributors who want to make code changes should set up a local development environment.

docs.title: 4.1 Requirements
docs.text:
Ensure the following are installed:

  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.3+
  • PHP extensions: pdo, pdo_mysql, json, mbstring, session, fileinfo, zip
  • Git

docs.title: 4.2 Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/GuiHui-huimy/LabPress.git
cd LabPress

docs.title: 4.3 Create a Local Database
docs.text:
mysql -u root -p -e "CREATE DATABASE labpress_dev CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;"
mysql -u root -p labpress_dev < labpressexample.sql

docs.title: 4.4 Configure the Database Connection
docs.text:
Copy the sample configuration, then set the database credentials for the local environment:

cp includes/config-sample.php includes/config.php

Keep the local configuration private. Do not commit changes to config.php if they contain real credentials.

docs.title: 4.5 Start the Local Server
docs.text:
Use the PHP built-in server:

php -S 127.0.0.1:8080

Then open:

http://127.0.0.1:8080

The admin panel is available at:

http://127.0.0.1:8080/admin

Default administrator credentials are provided by the sample database. Change them after first login.

docs.title: 5. Branching and Workflow
docs.text: Contributions should be made through feature branches and pull requests.

docs.title: 5.1 Fork the Repository
docs.text: If you do not have write access to the main repository, create a fork on GitHub and clone your fork.

docs.title: 5.2 Create a Feature Branch
docs.text:
Use a short, descriptive branch name:

git checkout -b fix-news-permission

Examples:

  • fix-upload-validation
  • add-plugin-hook
  • update-readme

docs.title: 5.3 Make Focused Changes
docs.text: Keep each pull request focused on one change or one logical group of changes. Avoid mixing unrelated modifications in the same branch.

docs.title: 5.4 Commit Messages
docs.text:
Use clear and descriptive commit messages. The first line should summarize the change. If necessary, add a blank line followed by a more detailed explanation.

Example:

Fix permission check in user management API

The PUT method now verifies that only users with the all
permission can modify other users. Self-service password
changes remain available for all authenticated users.

docs.title: 6. Code Standards
docs.text: LabPress is written in plain PHP, JavaScript, and CSS without external frameworks. Contributors should follow the existing style conventions.

docs.title: 6.1 PHP
docs.text:
• Use prepared statements for all database queries.
  • Escape output with htmlspecialchars() where user-visible data is rendered.
  • Use the short array syntax [].
  • Prefer clear function names and avoid abbreviations unless they are obvious.
  • Follow the existing code organization, placing shared functions in includes/functions.php and admin views in admin/views/.
  • Do not add third-party PHP dependencies unless absolutely necessary.

docs.title: 6.2 JavaScript
docs.text:
• Use plain JavaScript without framework dependencies.
  • Keep admin JavaScript files in admin/assets/js/ and frontend JavaScript in assets/js/.
  • Use descriptive variable names and avoid polluting the global namespace unless consistent with existing code.

docs.title: 6.3 CSS
docs.text:
• Follow the existing pattern of page-specific stylesheets.
  • Use CSS variables where the current theme supports them.
  • Avoid inline styles in templates unless the style is generated dynamically.

docs.title: 6.4 Language Files
docs.text:
When adding new interface strings:

  • Add the key to all existing language files.
  • Use descriptive keys and consistent naming.
  • For plugin language files, use a unique prefix to avoid conflicts with core keys.

docs.title: 6.5 Database Changes
docs.text:
If a change requires a new table or column:

  • Update the labpressexample.sql file so that new installations include the change.
  • Document the change in the relevant documentation page.
  • For plugin-specific tables, prefer creating tables during plugin activation rather than modifying the core SQL dump.

docs.title: 7. Testing
docs.text: Before submitting a pull request, perform basic testing.

docs.title: 7.1 Syntax Checks
docs.text:
Run PHP syntax checks on all changed files:

php -l path/to/changed-file.php

To check all PHP files:

find . -name "*.php" -exec php -l {} \;

docs.title: 7.2 Manual Testing
docs.text:
Manually verify the affected functionality. For example:

  • If the change affects login, test login and logout.
  • If the change affects content management, test creating and editing the relevant content type.
  • If the change affects plugins, test activation, deactivation, and uninstallation.
  • If the change affects translations, test both the admin and frontend language contexts.

docs.title: 7.3 No Automated Test Suite
docs.text: The project does not currently have a formal automated test suite. Manual testing is therefore the primary verification method for contributions.

docs.title: 8. Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation is an important part of the project. When adding or changing features, update the relevant documentation pages under docs/.

Documentation changes can be submitted as pull requests independently of code changes.

When writing documentation:

  • Use clear, concise English.
  • Follow the existing chapter and section structure.
  • Include code examples and screenshots where appropriate.
  • Keep technical descriptions accurate and aligned with the actual implementation.

docs.title: 9. Pull Requests
docs.text: Once your changes are ready, submit a pull request to the main repository.

docs.title: 9.1 Pull Request Checklist
docs.text:
Before submitting:

  • Ensure the branch is up to date with the main branch.
  • Run PHP syntax checks.
  • Test the change manually.
  • Update related documentation if necessary.
  • Avoid committing config.php with real credentials.
  • Do not include unrelated changes in the same pull request.

docs.title: 9.2 Pull Request Description
docs.text:
In the pull request description, explain:

  • What the change does.
  • Why the change is needed.
  • How the change was tested.
  • Any potential side effects or areas that need review.

docs.title: 9.3 Review Process
docs.text:
Maintainers will review the pull request and may request changes. After approval, the changes will be merged into the main branch.

Response times may vary. Keep the discussion professional and focused on the technical content.

docs.title: 10. License
docs.text:
By contributing to LabPress, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the same open-source license as the project. The project is released under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

See the LICENSE file for the full license text.

docs.title: 11. Next Steps
docs.text:
After reading this guide, you may want to:

  • Review the Developer Resources chapter for more detailed technical context.
  • Read the Plugin Development section if you plan to build a plugin.
  • Check the Hooks Reference before adding new hook-related functionality.
  • Explore the API Reference and Database Schema for technical details.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
This chapter describes the security measures implemented in LabPress and provides recommendations for running a LabPress site securely in production. It also explains how to report security vulnerabilities.

The information is intended for site administrators and developers. It covers the built-in protections, deployment considerations, and the process for responsible disclosure.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
LabPress includes several security controls that are designed to protect the application, its data, and its users during normal operation. These controls cover authentication, authorization, database access, output escaping, file uploads, and plugin management.

While LabPress includes these protections, no web application can be considered completely secure without a properly configured hosting environment. Administrators should follow the deployment recommendations in this chapter and keep the system up to date.

flowchart TD
    A[Request] --> B{Authenticated?}
    B -->|No| C[Redirect to login / 403]
    B -->|Yes| D{Required permission?}
    D -->|No| E[403 / denied view]
    D -->|Yes| F[Prepared statement / escaped output]
    F --> G[Upload or plugin action]
    G --> H[Audit and backup]

docs.title: 2.1 Password Storage
docs.text:
User passwords are never stored in plain text. LabPress uses PHP’s password_hash() function with the bcrypt algorithm to generate password hashes.

During login, the system verifies the supplied password with password_verify(). This ensures that passwords are stored in a format that is resistant to brute-force and precomputation attacks if the database is compromised.

docs.title: 2.2 Session-Based Authentication
docs.text:
Access to the admin panel is protected by PHP sessions. After a successful login, the user’s identity and permissions are stored in session variables.

All admin entry points verify that a valid session exists before allowing access. If the session is missing or invalid, the user is redirected to the login page or the API returns an authentication error.

The admin login process also supports a login_redirect_url filter, but authentication itself is enforced before any admin view is rendered.

docs.title: 2.3 Permission System
docs.text:
LabPress uses a role-based permission model for backend operations.

Each administrator account has a permissions field stored as a JSON array. Permissions are checked before:

  • Rendering admin pages.
  • Executing write operations through the API.
  • Performing sensitive actions such as plugin management, user management, and site configuration.

The hasPermission() function enforces these checks. Users with the all permission have full access. Other permissions allow only the corresponding module access.

docs.title: 2.4 Database Security
docs.text:
All database queries use PDO prepared statements with parameter binding. This prevents SQL injection by separating SQL logic from user-supplied values.

The database connection is configured with:

  • PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION
  • PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false

These settings ensure that errors are handled consistently and that prepared statements are not emulated in a way that could weaken their safety.

docs.title: 2.5 Output Escaping
docs.text:
User-generated content and data retrieved from the database are escaped before being rendered in HTML output.

The templates use htmlspecialchars() to escape dynamic values. This reduces the risk of cross-site scripting (XSS) when displaying content such as news titles, project names, menu items, and configuration values.

Markdown rendering uses the bundled Parsedown library with setSafeMode(false), which intentionally allows raw HTML inside Markdown bodies. That means article/project body content is trusted input, not sanitized input. Only administrators and editors you trust should be able to write long-form content; if that trust boundary is not acceptable, switch Parsedown to safe mode or add an HTML sanitizer before rendering.

The same principle applies to site_config values such as About Us text: some fields are intentionally rendered as HTML. Do not grant content permissions to accounts you would not trust with HTML output.

docs.title: 2.6 File Upload Restrictions
docs.text:
The image upload endpoint api/upload.php accepts only a defined set of image MIME types:

  • image/jpeg
  • image/png
  • image/gif
  • image/webp

Uploaded files are saved in the uploads/ directory under a subdirectory determined by the content type. The upload operation is restricted to authenticated users.

Plugin ZIP uploads are restricted to users with the all permission, and the installation process checks for the presence of a plugin.php file inside the uploaded archive.

docs.title: 2.7 Plugin Management Controls
docs.text:
Plugin management actions are restricted to users with the all permission. These actions include:

  • Plugin installation from ZIP
  • Plugin installation from a remote URL
  • Plugin activation and deactivation
  • Plugin uninstallation

The plugin uninstall process validates the plugin slug using a strict pattern that only permits letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens. This prevents path traversal through the plugin identifier.

docs.title: 2.8 Configuration Protection
docs.text:
The database configuration file includes/config.php contains sensitive credentials. It is not intended to be committed to version control.

The repository includes a .gitignore rule that excludes config.php. Administrators should verify that this file is not exposed publicly and that the web server is configured to deny direct access to PHP files inside the includes/ directory.

docs.title: 3.1 Use HTTPS
docs.text:
Enable HTTPS on the production server. HTTPS encrypts traffic between the browser and the server, protecting login credentials and session cookies from interception.

Most hosting panels, including BaoTa, provide tools for obtaining and installing free SSL certificates.

docs.title: 3.2 Change Default Credentials
docs.text:
The sample database includes a default administrator account. The credentials are publicly documented and must be changed immediately after installation.

Administrators should create strong, unique passwords and avoid reusing passwords across systems.

docs.title: 3.3 Restrict Access to Sensitive Directories
docs.text:
The following directories should not be publicly accessible through the web server:

  • includes/
  • plugins/ – except through the normal PHP loading process
  • api/ – if direct access is not required, restrict it to application-level routing

The web server should be configured to deny direct access to PHP files in these directories when appropriate.

docs.title: 3.4 Set Correct File Permissions
docs.text:
Directories that require write access from the PHP process should be configured with the minimum necessary permissions.

Typical recommended permissions:

chmod -R 755 uploads/
chmod -R 755 plugins/
chmod -R 755 images/

If the web server runs under a separate user such as www-data, ownership should be adjusted accordingly.

docs.title: 3.5 Keep the System Updated
docs.text:
Check the GitHub repository regularly for new releases and security updates. Apply updates in a timely manner.

Before performing an update, back up the database and the web directory. If the update requires manual file replacement, follow the release notes carefully.

docs.title: 3.6 Backup Regularly
docs.text:
Maintain regular backups of both the database and the uploads/ directory. Backups should be stored in a secure location outside the web root.

The most important data is stored in the MySQL database. Use the backup tools provided by your hosting panel or automated scripts to create periodic database dumps.

docs.title: 3.7 Use Trusted Plugins Only
docs.text:
Plugins can execute PHP code and therefore have full access to the server environment. Only install plugins from trusted sources.

Before activating a new plugin, review its code or ensure that it comes from a repository or author you trust.

docs.title: 4. Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability in LabPress, please report it privately. Do not open a public issue or disclose the details until the maintainers have had a chance to address the problem.

The full reporting process is described in the SECURITY.md file in the repository root.

When reporting a vulnerability, include:

  • A clear description of the vulnerability.
  • The affected version or commit.
  • Steps to reproduce the issue.
  • The potential impact.
  • Any suggested remediation, if available.

The maintainers will acknowledge the report and work with the reporter to validate and address the issue.

docs.title: 5. Known Security Boundaries
docs.text:
LabPress is designed for use by research groups and small laboratory teams. It is not intended to be exposed to untrusted, anonymous user registration or content submission.

The admin panel is restricted to trusted administrators. The public frontend is primarily read-oriented and does not allow public user registration or comment submission by default.

When deploying LabPress in a shared or public environment, treat the admin panel as the primary security boundary and restrict access to it using additional controls such as IP allowlists or VPN access if necessary.

docs.title: 6. Operational Checks
docs.text:
• The default root password has been changed.
  • includes/config.php is outside version control and not web-readable.
  • HTTPS is enabled and session cookies are marked HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
  • Only trusted users hold all or content-edit permissions.
  • uploads/, plugins/, and images/ are not directly executable.
  • Plugin ZIPs are reviewed before activation.
  • Database and uploads/ backups exist outside the web root.
  • Markdown raw-HTML behavior is accepted or safe mode is enabled.

docs.title: 7. Next Steps
docs.text:
After reviewing the security documentation, you may want to:

  • Read the Installation Guide for secure installation steps.
  • Review the Configuration Layers for environment settings.
  • Check the Users Management guide for account and permission best practices.
  • Review the Plugin Management guide for plugin safety.
  • Consult the Developer Resources if you are working with the codebase.

docs.title: Research News Management
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to manage research news and announcements in the LabPress administration panel. The News module is used to publish laboratory updates, research highlights, conference reports, and other time-sensitive content on the public website.

The guide focuses on practical operations. It describes how to create, edit, and delete news entries, how to format content using Markdown, how to attach images, and how news items are displayed on the frontend.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The News module stores each announcement as a record containing a title, summary, Markdown content, optional image, author, publication date, and display order. The public website presents news in two views: a list page and a detail page.

Each news item can include a featured image that appears alongside the summary in the list and at the top of the detail page. The content field supports Markdown, allowing you to format paragraphs, headings, lists, links, and code blocks without writing HTML.

All news data is stored in the news table. The admin panel provides a dedicated management page for maintaining news entries.

docs.title: 1.1 Data and publishing workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Add or Edit News modal] --> B[Markdown content]
    B --> C[api/save.php<br/>type=news]
    C --> D[(news table)]
    D --> E[news.php list]
    D --> F[news-detail.php]
    E --> G[news_list_title / news_list_summary filters]
    F --> H[the_content filter]

The list page and the detail page both read the same record. There is no separate “draft” state in the current module: saving a news item makes it part of the public list immediately.

Figure 1. The Research News manager. The list is ordered by date and then sort value.

docs.title: 2. Accessing the News Manager
docs.text:
The News manager is available from the admin sidebar under Research News. In the admin menu, this page is labeled Research News or News, depending on the active language.

Access to the news manager requires the publications permission. Administrator accounts with the all permission can also access it. Users without the required permission will see a permission error message.

To open the page, click Research News in the sidebar. The page displays a table containing all existing news entries, ordered by date and sort value.

docs.title: 3. Understanding the News List
docs.text:
The news list shows the following columns:

  • Title – the headline of the news item.
  • Date – the publication date as stored in the database.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the entry.

The list is sorted by date descending and then by the sort order field. This means the most recent news appears at the top. The public news page follows the same ordering rule.

If no news entries have been added, the page displays a “No data” message.

Figure 2. News list. The newest date is not automatically the top item when another item has a stronger sort value in the same date group.

docs.title: 4. Adding a News Item
docs.text:
To add a new news item:

  1. Open the Research News page.
  2. Click the Add News button at the top of the table.
  3. In the modal form that appears, fill in the fields described below.

The news form includes the following fields:

Field Description Title The headline of the news item. This field is required. Summary A short summary displayed in the news list. This field is recommended. Content The full article content, written in Markdown. Optional, but recommended for detail pages. Image An optional image displayed with the news item. Use the upload button to attach an image. Author The author or source of the news, for example a professor’s name or the lab name. Date The publication date. This field is required.
  1. Click Save.

The new news item is inserted into the database and appears immediately in the admin list and on the public news page.

docs.title: 4.1 Writing Markdown Content
docs.text:
The content field uses a Markdown editor. You can write formatted text without knowing HTML. The editor provides a toolbar with common formatting buttons, including bold, italic, headings, quotes, lists, links, images, and code blocks.

Common formatting examples include:

  • Use # Heading for headings.
  • Use **bold** for emphasis.
  • Use - item for bullet lists.
  • Use [link text](https://example.com) for links.
  • Use triple backticks for code blocks.

The public news detail page automatically converts Markdown to HTML when displaying the content.

Figure 3. The Markdown editor in the news modal. Formatting is stored as Markdown and converted by Parsedown on the detail page.

docs.title: 4.2 Uploading a News Image
docs.text:
The image field includes an upload button. To attach an image:

  1. Click the Upload button next to the image field.
  2. Select an image file from your computer.
  3. The system uploads the image to the uploads/news/ directory.
  4. A preview appears in the form.

The image will be shown as a thumbnail in the news list and as a featured image at the top of the news detail page. If no image is uploaded, the news item will still display correctly, with only text content.

docs.title: 5. Editing a News Item
docs.text:
To modify an existing news item:

  1. Find the entry you want to change in the news list.
  2. Click the Edit button in that row.
  3. The same modal form opens with the current values filled in.
  4. Update any field, including the Markdown content or image.
  5. Click Save.

The changes are saved immediately and reflected on the public website after the next page load.

Figure 4. Editing an existing item. The current Markdown and image path are loaded into the same modal.

docs.title: 6. Deleting a News Item
docs.text:
To remove a news item:

  1. Find the entry in the news list.
  2. Click the Delete button in that row.
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

The news item is permanently removed from the database. The associated image file may remain in the uploads directory, but the item will no longer appear on the website.

If you want to temporarily hide a news item without deleting it, consider changing its date to an older value or editing the content to indicate that the item is no longer current, as there is no separate visibility switch in this module.

docs.title: 7. Controlling Date and Display Order
docs.text:
The public news list is sorted by the Date field, with the most recent dates appearing first. The sort order field is also considered, but its practical use is limited because date ordering usually dominates.

To control the display order of news items, set the Date field appropriately when creating or editing an entry. For example, if you want an item to appear at the top, assign it a more recent date.

If you need to pin an important announcement to the top regardless of its date, you can adjust the sort order value and, if necessary, modify the frontend template to prioritize sort order over date. By default, the current implementation prioritizes date descending.

docs.title: 8. Frontend Display
docs.text: News items are displayed in two public views.

docs.title: 8.1 News List Page
docs.text:
The public Research News page lists all news entries. Each entry shows:

  • The news image, if available.
  • The title as a clickable link to the detail page.
  • The author and date.
  • A short summary.
  • A “Read More” button linking to the full article.

The list is rendered by news.php and uses the news_list_title and news_list_summary filters before output. This allows plugins to modify the displayed text if needed.

Figure 5. The public news list. Images, titles, authors, dates, and summaries are rendered from the same record.

docs.title: 8.2 News Detail Page
docs.text:
Clicking a news title opens the detail page. This page displays the full Markdown-rendered content, the featured image if present, the author, and the date. A back link returns to the news list.

The detail page applies the page_title filter to the news title and the the_content filter to the rendered Markdown content. These filters allow plugins such as Dynamic Multi-Language or custom plugins to modify the output.

Figure 6. The public detail page. The Markdown body is rendered to HTML and filtered through the_content.

docs.title: 9. Multilingual Considerations
docs.text:
News titles, summaries, and content are stored as raw text in the database. The core does not automatically translate news content.

If your site needs news in multiple languages, consider these options:

  • Publish news in a single primary language, such as English or Chinese, while the rest of the site interface remains multilingual.
  • Write bilingual news content by including both languages in the Markdown body, separated by headings or paragraphs.
  • Use custom plugins or filters to translate news titles and summaries if multilingual news support becomes a requirement. The news_list_title and news_list_summary filters are available for this purpose.

The Dynamic Multi-Language plugin does not currently provide a dedicated translation tab for news content, but its filter system can be extended to support news fields if needed.

docs.title: 10. Operational Checks
docs.text:
• Title, date, summary, and Markdown body are all present before publishing.
  • The date is in the expected time zone and format.
  • Images exist under uploads/news/ and are readable.
  • The detail page renders Markdown links and code blocks correctly.
  • The list ordering matches the intended date/sort policy.
  • The item is not being cached with an older version on the frontend.

If a news item is missing from the public list, check the date value and the query limit before assuming a failed save. If the detail page is empty, inspect the stored content field and confirm that Markdown is being passed to Parsedown.

docs.title: 11. Next Steps
docs.text:
After managing research news, you may want to continue with:

  • Publications – manage academic publications.
  • Slides – manage homepage carousel slides.
  • Tools – manage bioinformatics tools and software.
  • Projects – manage research projects.
  • Site Settings – configure homepage sections that display news and other content.

docs.title: Projects Management
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to manage research projects and project categories in the LabPress administration panel. The Projects module is designed to present research activities, software development, or laboratory initiatives in a structured and visually organized manner on the public website.

The guide focuses on practical operations. It describes how to create project categories, add and maintain project entries, control homepage featured projects, and understand how projects are displayed on the frontend.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
LabPress organizes projects into categories and presents them using a filterable list and individual detail pages. Each project can include a title, summary, detailed Markdown content, an image, external links, and a featured flag that controls whether the project appears on the homepage.

Project management is divided into two admin pages:

  • Project Categories – manages the categories used to group projects.
  • Project List – manages individual project entries and their display order.

Both pages are accessible from the Projects parent menu in the admin sidebar.

docs.title: 1.1 Data model and publishing workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    C[Project Categories<br/>slug, name, description] --> CT[(project_categories)]
    P[Project List<br/>title, summary, Markdown, image, featured] --> PT[(projects)]
    CT --> PT
    PT --> API[api/data.php?type=projects]
    API --> LIST[projects.php list + category filter]
    API --> HOME[Homepage featured projects]
    PT --> DETAIL[project-detail.php]

A project belongs to one category. The category slug is the filter key used by the public projects page. The featured flag is independent of sort order: featured controls whether the homepage section includes the item; sort order controls the sequence within lists.

Figure 1. The Project Categories table and the Projects submenu. Always create the category before assigning a project to it.

docs.title: 2. Accessing the Projects Module
docs.text:
To manage projects, click Projects in the admin sidebar. A submenu appears with two entries:

  • Project Categories
  • Project List

Access to these pages requires the tools permission. Administrator accounts with the all permission can also access them. Users without the appropriate permission will see a permission error message.

docs.title: 3. Managing Project Categories
docs.text: Project categories allow you to group related projects and provide a way for visitors to filter the project list on the public site.

docs.title: 3.1 Understanding the Category List
docs.text:
The Project Categories page displays a table with the following columns:

  • Slug – a short English identifier used in URLs.
  • Name – the display name of the category.
  • Description – a brief explanation of the category, shown on the public category page.
  • Sort – the display order of the category.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the category.

The category list is ordered by the sort_order field.

Figure 2. Category list. Category slugs are stable filter keys; changing a slug can break existing links.

docs.title: 3.2 Adding a Category
docs.text:
To add a new category:

  1. Open Projects > Project Categories.
  2. Click the Add Category button.
  3. In the modal form, fill in the following fields:
Field Description Slug A unique English identifier, for example deep-learning or structural-biology. Use lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, or underscores. This field is required. Name The display name, such as Deep Learning or Structural Biology. This field is required. Description A short description of the category. This text may be displayed on the category detail page. Sort A numeric value that controls the order in which categories appear in the sidebar and filter buttons. Lower values appear first.
  1. Click Save.

The new category is inserted into the project_categories table and becomes available for use when creating projects.

Figure 3. Add Category. Use a lowercase slug with hyphens or underscores; avoid changing it after projects reference it.

docs.title: 3.3 Editing and Deleting Categories
docs.text:
Each category row has Edit and Delete buttons.

Editing opens the modal with the current values filled in. You can update the slug, name, description, or sort order and save the changes.

Deleting a category permanently removes it from the database. Before deleting, ensure that no projects are assigned to the category, because the database may prevent deletion if projects still reference the category. If you need to remove a category that is in use, first reassign its projects to another category.

docs.title: 4. Managing the Project List
docs.text: The Project List page is the main interface for managing project entries. It shows all projects in a paginated table and provides controls for adding, editing, and deleting projects.

docs.title: 4.1 Understanding the Project List
docs.text:
The project list displays the following columns:

  • Image – a small thumbnail of the project image.
  • Title – the project title.
  • Category – the assigned category name.
  • Sort – the display order value.
  • Featured – whether the project is shown on the homepage.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the project.

The list is paginated, showing twelve projects per page by default. Use the pagination controls at the bottom of the table to navigate through the list.

docs.title: 4.2 Adding a Project
docs.text:
To add a new project:

  1. Open Projects > Project List.
  2. Click the Add Project button.
  3. In the modal form, fill in the fields described below.

The project form includes the following fields:

Field Description Title The name of the project. This field is required. Summary A short description shown in list cards. This field is optional but recommended. Content The detailed project description, written in Markdown. Image A representative image for the project. Use the upload button to select an image. Category The category to which the project belongs. This field is required. GitHub URL Optional link to the project’s source code repository. Documentation URL Optional link to the documentation or manual. External URL Optional link to a project website or related page. Sort A numeric value that controls the display order. Lower values appear first. Featured Select Yes to show the project on the homepage, or No to hide it from the homepage.
  1. Click Save.

The project is inserted into the projects table and appears in the project list and on the public projects page. If featured, it may also appear on the homepage.

docs.title: 4.3 Writing Project Content in Markdown
docs.text:
The project content field uses Markdown for formatting. You can write headings, paragraphs, lists, code blocks, tables, and links. The public project detail page automatically converts Markdown to HTML using the bundled Parsedown library.

For example, a project description may include:

  • A short introduction paragraph.
  • A section explaining the background or motivation.
  • A list of key features.
  • A code block for command examples.
  • Links to external documentation or papers.

The Markdown editor in the admin form provides basic toolbar buttons for formatting, preview, and split-screen editing.

Figure 4. The project editor. The content field is Markdown; EasyMDE supplies the toolbar and preview controls.

The Markdown editor in the admin form provides basic toolbar buttons for formatting, preview, and split-screen editing. The editor is a convenience layer; the stored value is plain Markdown.

docs.title: 4.4 Uploading a Project Image
docs.text:
The project form includes an image upload control. To add or change the project image:

  1. Click the Upload button next to the image field.
  2. Select an image file from your computer.
  3. The system uploads the image to the uploads/projects/ directory.
  4. A preview appears in the form.

Supported image types include JPG, PNG, GIF, and WebP. The uploaded image is displayed in the project list card and on the project detail page.

docs.title: 4.5 Editing a Project
docs.text:
To edit an existing project:

  1. Find the project in the project list.
  2. Click the Edit button in that row.
  3. The modal opens with the current values filled in.
  4. Update any field, including the category, featured status, or Markdown content.
  5. Click Save.

The changes take effect immediately and are reflected on the frontend after the next page load.

docs.title: 4.6 Deleting a Project
docs.text:
To delete a project:

  1. Find the project in the project list.
  2. Click the Delete button in that row.
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

The project is permanently removed from the database. This operation cannot be undone. If you want to temporarily remove a project from display, consider changing its featured status or sort order instead of deleting it.

docs.title: 5. Controlling Display Order
docs.text:
Project order is controlled by the Sort field. Lower values appear earlier in the list.

The public projects page orders projects by sort_order ascending, followed by creation date descending for projects with the same sort value. It is recommended to use increments of ten (10, 20, 30) for easier insertion of new projects later.

To reorder projects, edit each project and adjust its sort value.

docs.title: 6. Frontend Display
docs.text: Projects are displayed in three public areas: the homepage featured section, the projects listing page, and the project detail page.

docs.title: 6.1 Homepage Featured Projects
docs.text: The homepage displays featured projects in a section titled Projects and Achievements. Only projects with featured = 1 appear here. The section shows a limited number of featured projects, typically eight, in a row-style layout with image, category, title, summary, and links.

docs.title: 6.2 Projects Listing Page
docs.text:
The public Projects page includes a left sidebar with category filters and a main content area listing projects. Visitors can click a category to filter the displayed projects. Each project row shows the image, category tag, title, summary, and action links.

The page also includes pagination for projects when the total number exceeds the page size.

Figure 5. The public projects page. Category selection filters the list; the sidebar is generated from project categories.

docs.title: 6.3 Project Detail Page
docs.text:
The project detail page displays the full Markdown-rendered content, featured image, category tag, and external links. The page title and content are filterable by plugins.

A prominent button row at the bottom provides links to the GitHub repository, documentation, and any external project page if those URLs are set.

Figure 6. The project detail page. Markdown is rendered to HTML; GitHub, documentation, and external links are shown only when configured.

docs.title: 7. Multilingual Considerations
docs.text:
Project titles, summaries, and content are stored as raw text in the database. The core does not automatically translate project data.

If you need multilingual project content, consider the following:

  • Maintain project content in a single primary language, such as English, while the site interface remains multilingual.
  • Store bilingual text within the Markdown content using headings to separate language sections.
  • Use the Dynamic Multi-Language plugin’s filters or custom plugins to translate project titles or summaries if required.

The project list and detail templates apply filters such as project_list_title and project_list_summary, which can be extended by developers for translation purposes.

docs.title: 8. Operational Checks
docs.text:
• Every project has a category whose slug still exists.
  • Featured projects are limited enough for the homepage layout (the template requests eight).
  • Sort values are consistent across categories; a new project's position is intentional.
  • Markdown links and images render correctly on the detail page.
  • Deleting a category does not leave orphaned projects.
  • A project image exists under uploads/projects/ and is readable by the web server.

If a project disappears from the homepage, check the featured flag before checking the template. If a category filter is empty, confirm that the project's category_id points to an existing category and that the slug is URL-safe.

docs.title: 9. Next Steps
docs.text:
After managing projects, you may want to continue with:

  • Tools – manage bioinformatics tools and software.
  • Publications – manage academic publications.
  • Slides – manage homepage carousel slides.
  • Research News – manage laboratory news.
  • Site Settings – configure homepage sections that include featured projects.

docs.title: Publications Management
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to manage publication entries in the LabPress administration panel. Publications are used to display research papers, journal articles, and other academic outputs on the public website.

The guide focuses on practical operations. It describes how to add, edit, delete, and organize publication records through the admin interface, and how these records appear on the frontend.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The Publications module provides a simple way to maintain a list of papers and journal articles. Each publication consists of a title, authors, journal name, external link, and sort order. These entries are displayed on the public Publications page and are also used in the Latest Publications section of the homepage.

All publication data is stored in the publications table. The admin panel provides a dedicated management page that allows administrators to maintain the list without editing the database directly.

Figure 1. The Publications manager. The table is read directly from the publications table.

docs.title: 2. Accessing the Publications Manager
docs.text:
The Publications manager is available from the admin sidebar under Publications.

Access to this page requires the publications permission. Administrator accounts with the all permission can also access it. Users without the required permission will see a permission error message.

To open the page, click Publications in the sidebar. The page displays a table containing all existing publication entries.

docs.title: 3. Publication Workflow at a Glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Add or Edit modal] --> B[api/save.php<br/>type=publications]
    B --> C[(publications table)]
    C --> D[Admin list]
    C --> E[publications.php]
    C --> F[Homepage Latest Publications]
    E --> G[publication_list_title filter]
    D --> H[Next page load]

The important consequence is that the admin list is not a separate cache. A successful save updates the table; the public page reflects it on the next request.

docs.title: 4. Understanding the Publication List
docs.text:
The publication list shows the following columns:

  • Title – the title of the paper or article.
  • Authors – the list of authors as stored in the database.
  • Journal – the name of the journal or publication venue.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the entry.

The list is ordered by the sort_order field, with lower values appearing first. Entries with the same sort order may appear in the order they were inserted.

If no publications have been added, the page displays a “No data” message.

Figure 2. The list view. The Edit action opens the same modal used for creation.

docs.title: 5. Adding a Publication
docs.text:
To add a new publication:

  1. Open the Publications page.
  2. Click the Add Publication button at the top of the table.
  3. In the modal form that appears, fill in the following fields:
Field Description Title The title of the publication. This field is required. Authors The author list, for example Zhang San, Li Si, Wang Wu. This field is required. Journal The journal or conference name. This field is required. Link An optional external URL, such as a DOI link or publisher page. Sort A numeric value that determines the display order. Lower values appear first.
  1. Click Save.

The new entry is inserted into the database and immediately appears in the publication list and on the public website.

Figure 3. The add/edit modal. Title, Authors, and Journal are required; Link and Sort are optional.

docs.title: 5.1 Field behavior and validation
docs.text:
Field Required Behavior Title Yes Trimmed text; HTML is escaped on output. Authors Yes Free text; commas are display separators, not a structured author list. Journal Yes Free text; no journal-name normalization is performed. Link No Stored as a URL; an empty value omits the public action link. Sort No Integer; lower values sort first. Default is 0.

The form does not validate DOI syntax or author order. Use a consistent internal convention (for example “Family Name, Given Name”) if the list is consumed by other systems.

docs.title: 6. Editing a Publication
docs.text:
To modify an existing publication:

  1. Find the entry you want to change in the publication list.
  2. Click the Edit button in that row.
  3. The same modal form opens with the current values filled in.
  4. Update the title, authors, journal, link, or sort order.
  5. Click Save.

The changes are saved immediately and reflected on the frontend after the next page load.

docs.title: 7. Deleting a Publication
docs.text:
To remove a publication:

  1. Find the entry in the publication list.
  2. Click the Delete button in that row.
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

The entry is permanently removed from the database. There is no undo, so use this operation with care.

If a publication should no longer be displayed but you want to keep the record for future use, consider changing its sort order or temporarily removing the public link instead of deleting it.

docs.title: 8. Controlling Display Order
docs.text:
The display order of publications is controlled by the Sort field. Lower values appear first.

The homepage and the public Publications page query the database using the following ordering rule:

ORDER BY sort_order ASC

This means that a publication with sort order 0 will appear before one with sort order 10.

When adding several new publications, it is useful to assign sort values in increments of ten, such as 10, 20, 30. This leaves space to insert additional entries later without renumbering the entire list.

To reorder publications, edit each entry and change its sort value as needed.

docs.title: 9. Frontend Display
docs.text: Publication entries are displayed in two public locations.

docs.title: 9.1 Publications Page
docs.text:
The public Publications page lists all publication entries in a simple, readable format. Each entry shows the title, authors, and journal. If an external link is provided, a button labeled Read or Read More links to the original article or DOI.

The page uses the publications.php template and applies the publication_list_title filter to each title before rendering. This allows plugins to modify the displayed title if necessary.

docs.title: 9.2 Homepage Latest Publications
docs.text:
The homepage also shows a limited number of recent publications in the Latest Publications section. The homepage loads publications asynchronously from the API and displays only the first five entries.

The homepage section includes a View More button that links to the full Publications page.

Figure 4. The public publications page. The title is filtered through publication_list_title before output.

docs.title: 10. Multilingual Considerations
docs.text:
Publication titles, author lists, and journal names are stored as raw text in the database. The current core does not translate these fields automatically.

If you need to display publications in multiple languages, you have two practical options:

  • Store the publication information in the desired primary language and let the rest of the site switch languages while the publication details remain unchanged.
  • Use a plugin or custom filter to manage translations for publication titles if multilingual publication display becomes a requirement.

The Dynamic Multi-Language plugin does not currently provide a dedicated translation tab for publications, but custom translations can be extended through the plugin’s filter system if needed.

docs.title: 11. Operational Checks
docs.text:
Before considering a publication entry complete:

  • Title, authors, and journal are present.
  • The external link opens the intended DOI or publisher page.
  • The sort value follows the site's numbering convention.
  • The public list shows the entry in the expected position.
  • The homepage "Latest Publications" block shows the item if it belongs in the newest set.

If a save appears to succeed but the public page does not change, check the response from api/save.php, the publications table, and any page cache in front of the site. The admin table reads the database directly; a stale public page is usually a caching layer, not a failed insert.

docs.title: 12. Next Steps
docs.text:
After managing publications, you may want to continue with:

  • Slides – manage homepage carousel slides.
  • Tools – manage bioinformatics tools and software.
  • Projects – manage research projects and portfolios.
  • Research News – manage laboratory news and announcements.
  • Site Settings – configure the homepage sections that display publications.

docs.title: Slides Management
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to manage homepage slides in the LabPress administration panel. Slides are the large banner images displayed in the rotating carousel at the top of the homepage.

The guide focuses on practical operations: adding, editing, deleting, and ordering slides through the admin interface. It also describes how slides are loaded on the frontend and how multilingual content can be applied.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The Slides module controls the homepage carousel. Each slide consists of an image, a title, a short description, and a sort order. The homepage displays these slides as a rotating banner with automatic transition and manual navigation indicators.

All slide data is stored in the slides table. The admin panel provides a dedicated management page that allows administrators to maintain the carousel content without editing the database directly.

Figure 1. The Slides manager. Each row corresponds to one carousel record.

docs.title: 2. Accessing the Slides Manager
docs.text:
The Slides manager is available from the admin sidebar under Slides.

Access to this page requires the slides permission. Administrator accounts with the all permission can also access it. Users without the required permission will see a permission error message.

To open the page, click Slides in the sidebar. The page displays a table containing all existing slides.

docs.title: 3. Slide Workflow at a Glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Add or Edit modal] --> B[api/upload.php]
    B --> C[uploads/slides/]
    A --> D[api/save.php<br/>type=slides]
    D --> E[(slides table)]
    E --> F[index.php carousel]
    E --> G[api/data.php?type=slides]
    G --> F

The slide record stores the image path, title, description, and sort order. The carousel uses the API as its data source; the static markup in index.php is only a fallback for an empty or unavailable API response.

docs.title: 4. Understanding the Slide List
docs.text:
The slide list shows the following columns:

  • Preview – a small thumbnail of the slide image.
  • Title – the main heading displayed on the slide.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the slide.

The list is ordered by the sort_order field, with lower values appearing first in the carousel. If no slides have been added, the page displays a “No data” message.

Figure 2. The list view. Thumbnails are loaded from the stored image path; a missing file produces a broken preview.

docs.title: 5. Adding a Slide
docs.text:
To add a new slide:

  1. Open the Slides page.
  2. Click the Add Slide button at the top of the table.
  3. In the modal form that appears, fill in the following fields:
Field Description Title The main heading displayed on the slide. This field is required. Description A short supporting text displayed below the title. This field is required. Image The background image for the slide. Upload an image using the file picker. Sort A numeric value that controls the order of the slide in the carousel. Lower values appear first.
  1. Click Save.

The new slide is inserted into the database and will appear in the homepage carousel after the next page load.

docs.title: 5.1 Uploading a Slide Image
docs.text:
The slide form includes an image upload field. When you select an image file, the browser uploads it to the server through the api/upload.php endpoint.

The upload process:

  1. Select an image file from your computer.
  2. The system uploads the image to the uploads/slides/ directory.
  3. If the upload succeeds, a preview is displayed in the form.
  4. The image path is stored in the hidden form field.

Supported image types include JPG, PNG, GIF, and WebP. The maximum file size is determined by the server’s PHP configuration.

Figure 3. The add form. Uploading an image writes to uploads/slides/ and stores the returned path in the form.

docs.title: 6. Editing a Slide
docs.text:
To modify an existing slide:

  1. Find the slide you want to change in the slide list.
  2. Click the Edit button in that row.
  3. The same modal form opens with the current values filled in.
  4. Update the title, description, image, or sort order.
  5. Click Save.

If you need to replace the existing image, use the file picker to upload a new image. The new image will replace the previous one after saving.

Figure 4. The edit form. Replacing the image only changes the record after the modal is saved.

docs.title: 7. Deleting a Slide
docs.text:
To remove a slide:

  1. Find the slide in the slide list.
  2. Click the Delete button in that row.
  3. Confirm the deletion when prompted.

The slide is permanently removed from the database. The image file itself may remain in the uploads directory, but the slide will no longer be shown in the carousel.

If you want to temporarily hide a slide without deleting it, consider changing its sort order to a very high value or replacing its content later, as there is currently no separate active/inactive switch in this module.

docs.title: 8. Controlling Slide Order
docs.text:
The order of slides is controlled by the Sort field. Lower values appear earlier in the carousel.

The homepage loads slides using the following database query:

SELECT id, image, title, description FROM slides ORDER BY sort_order ASC

The carousel then cycles through the slides in this order. To rearrange slides, edit each slide and adjust its sort value. It is recommended to use increments of ten (10, 20, 30, etc.) so that future insertions are easier.

docs.title: 9. Frontend Display
docs.text:
The homepage carousel is rendered by index.php and the JavaScript file assets/js/index.js.

The frontend attempts to load slide data asynchronously from the API endpoint api/data.php?type=slides. If the API returns slides, the JavaScript dynamically builds the carousel HTML and replaces any static fallback slides.

Each slide is displayed with its title and description overlaid on the background image. The carousel automatically advances every few seconds and includes navigation indicators that users can click to jump to a specific slide.

If the API request fails or no slides are found, the frontend falls back to the static slides defined in the homepage HTML. However, the static slides are only a fallback and should not be relied upon for production content.

Figure 5. The frontend carousel. The API supplies slide data; the carousel advances automatically and supports indicator navigation.

docs.title: 10. Multilingual Support
docs.text:
Slide titles and descriptions are stored as raw text in the database. The Dynamic Multi-Language plugin can translate these fields without modifying the original content.

The plugin registers the slides_data filter, which is applied when the homepage loads slide data. It retrieves translations from the ml_translations table and replaces the title and description if a translation exists for the current locale.

To manage slide translations:

  1. Open the Dynamic Multi-Language admin page.
  2. Go to the Slides tab.
  3. For each slide, enter the translated title and description for the target language.
  4. Save the translations.

When the frontend language is switched, the translated slide content appears automatically.

Figure 6. Slide titles and descriptions are edited in the plugin's Slides tab; the original record remains untouched.

docs.title: 11. Operational Checks
docs.text:
• Every slide has a readable image path under uploads/slides/.
  • The title and description fit the carousel overlay at mobile and desktop widths.
  • The sort order is unique enough that the intended first slide is deterministic.
  • The API returns the same number of slides as the admin list.
  • The static fallback is not being mistaken for live content.

If the carousel shows old content after saving, check the browser cache and any page cache before changing the database. If it shows no slides, request api/data.php?type=slides directly and inspect the JSON response.

docs.title: 12. Next Steps
docs.text:
After managing slides, you may want to continue with:

  • Publications – manage academic publications.
  • Tools – manage bioinformatics tools and software.
  • Projects – manage research projects.
  • Research News – manage laboratory news.
  • Site Settings – configure the homepage sections that work together with the slides.

docs.title: Tools Management
docs.text:
This chapter explains how to manage bioinformatics tools and software in the LabPress administration panel. The Tools module is designed for laboratories that develop or maintain computational tools, databases, or software packages and want to present them professionally on the public website.

LabPress divides tool management into three related areas:

  • Tool List – manages the basic information for each tool.
  • Tool Detail – manages the extended description, metadata, and citation information.
  • Version History – records multiple versions and download links for each tool.

These three areas are accessed through the Tools parent menu in the admin sidebar. The following sections describe each area in a practical, task-oriented manner.

docs.title: 1.1 Data model at a glance
docs.text:
The module uses three related tables rather than one large tool record:

flowchart LR
    A[Tool List<br/>name, type, summary] --> T[(tools)]
    B[Tool Detail<br/>description, metadata, citation] --> TD[(tool_details)]
    C[Version History<br/>changes, downloads] --> TV[(tool_versions)]
    T --> API[api/data.php<br/>type=tools]
    TD --> API2[api/data.php<br/>type=tool-detail]
    TV --> API3[api/data.php<br/>type=tool-versions]
    API --> FRONT[Tools page / Tool detail page]
    API2 --> FRONT
    API3 --> FRONT

A tool can exist without a detail record or version records. The reverse is not true: detail and version rows are attached to a tool identifier. For that reason, create the tool first, then its detail, then its versions.

Figure 1. The Tools entry in the admin sidebar expands into Tool List, Tool Detail, and Version History.

docs.title: 1. Accessing the Tools Module
docs.text:
To manage tools, hover over or click Tools in the admin sidebar. A submenu appears with the following entries:

  • Tool List
  • Tool Detail
  • Version History

Click the corresponding submenu item to open the desired management page.

Access to all tool management pages requires the tools permission. Administrator accounts with the all permission can also access them. Users without the appropriate permission will see a permission error message.

docs.title: 2. Managing the Tool List
docs.text: The Tool List page is the starting point for managing tools. It displays all existing tools in a table and allows you to add new tools, edit basic information, and delete tools that are no longer needed.

docs.title: 2.1 Understanding the Tool List
docs.text:
The table contains the following columns:

  • Name – the display name of the tool.
  • Type – the tool category, either “Software” or “Database”.
  • Description – a short summary of the tool, truncated for display.
  • Actions – buttons for editing and deleting the tool.

The list is ordered by the sort_order field, which you can set when creating or editing a tool. Lower values appear earlier on the frontend.

Figure 2. Tool List. The table is the entry point for creating the record that detail and version pages attach to.

docs.title: 2.2 Adding a Tool
docs.text:
To add a new tool:

  1. Open Tools > Tool List.
  2. Click the Add Tool button at the top of the table.
  3. In the modal form, fill in the following fields:
Field Description Name The unique name of the tool. This field is required. Type Select Software or Database. Icon Class A Font Awesome icon class, for example fas fa-cut or fas fa-cube. Optional. Description A concise summary of the tool. This field is required. Features A short list of key features or capabilities. Optional. GitHub The GitHub repository URL. Optional. Website The official website or project page. Optional. Detail Link A custom link to the tool detail page. By default, this can be set to # or a specific URL. Sort A numeric value that controls the display order. Lower values appear first.
  1. Click Save.

The new tool is inserted into the tools table and appears immediately in the tool list and on the public tools page.

Figure 3. Add Tool. The detail link can be left as a placeholder until the tool detail page exists.

docs.title: 2.3 Editing a Tool
docs.text:
To edit an existing tool:

  1. Find the tool in the list.
  2. Click the Edit button in that row.
  3. The modal form opens with the current information filled in.
  4. Update any field as needed.
  5. Click Save.

The changes take effect immediately and are reflected on the frontend after the next page load.

docs.title: 2.4 Deleting a Tool
docs.text:
To delete a tool:

  1. Find the tool in the list.
  2. Click the Delete button in that row.
  3. Confirm the deletion.

The tool record is permanently removed. Associated tool detail and version history records may also be affected depending on the database foreign key constraints. Use this operation carefully.

docs.title: 3. Managing Tool Details
docs.text: The Tool Detail page allows you to manage the extended information that appears on the tool’s detail page. This includes a detailed description, version, programming language, license, update date, external links, images, and citation information.

docs.title: 3.1 Selecting a Tool
docs.text:
When you open Tools > Tool Detail, the page displays a dropdown list of all tools. Select a tool from the list to load its current detail information.

If no detail record exists for the selected tool, the form appears empty, and you can create a new detail record by filling in the fields and saving.

Figure 4. Tool Detail. Select a tool first; the form then loads an existing detail record or starts an empty one.

docs.title: 3.2 Tool Detail Fields
docs.text:
The tool detail form contains the following fields:

Field Description Short Description A brief summary shown at the top of the tool detail page. Detailed Description The main description content. This field supports HTML. Version The current version number of the tool. Programming Language The primary language used to develop the tool, such as Python, C++, or R. License The software license, for example GPL-3.0 or MIT. Update Date The last update date of the tool. GitHub The GitHub repository URL. Documentation The documentation or readthedocs URL. Homepage The official homepage or project page URL. Image An image or logo path for the tool. Screenshot A screenshot of the tool interface. Citation Title The title of the citation or publication to cite when using the tool. Citation URL The DOI or URL of the citation.

The detailed description supports HTML, allowing you to format paragraphs, lists, headings, and links. You can also include images directly in the HTML content.

To save the detail information, click Save at the bottom of the form.

Figure 5. The extended detail form. Field values are stored separately from the tool-list summary.

docs.title: 3.3 Updating Tool Details
docs.text: If a tool already has a detail record, selecting it from the dropdown loads the existing data into the form. You can update any field and save the changes. The updated information appears on the public tool detail page immediately.

docs.title: 4. Managing Version History
docs.text: The Version History page allows you to track multiple versions of a tool and provide download links for each version. This is useful for software releases, updates, and changelogs.

docs.title: 4.1 Selecting a Tool
docs.text:
When you open Tools > Version History, the page displays a dropdown list of all tools. Select a tool to load its version records.

If the selected tool has no versions, the page displays a message such as “No version records”.

Figure 6. Version History. The page is tool-scoped after a tool is selected from the dropdown.

docs.title: 4.2 Viewing Version Records
docs.text:
The version list shows each version with its number, release date, changes, and download links. Changes are displayed as bullet points, and downloads are shown as clickable links.

The page also includes an Add Version button to create a new version record.
